body:
There were only two consumers (the retrans table and exchanges) left, which both
used to fail unit tests if using ObjectPool due to use-after-free.

One of those tests is now fixed; the other is fixed in this PR.  So we can move
to using ObjectPool everywhere.

Fixes https://github.com/project-chip/connectedhomeip/issues/14509
Fixes https://github.com/project-chip/connectedhomeip/issues/14446

#### Problem
We have use-after-free that is being covered up by using pool allocation.

#### Change overview
Fix the use-after-free in WriteHandler, switch to ObjectPool for the last BitMapObjectPool holdouts.

#### Testing
Should pass CI.

author: ashleemboyer
body:
## 🔗 Relevant links

<!--
Include links to the branch preview, Asana task, and Figma designs wherever possible to make reviewing your PR easier.
When including the preview link, make sure to remove any '.' characters from the branch name:
  - Example: ks.my-branch -> ksmy-branch
-->

- [Preview link](https://dev-portal-git-ambuse-tabs-instead-of-spaces-hashicorp.vercel.app/) 🔎
- Relevant Asana Task: [Switch to tabs for accessibility concerns](https://app.asana.com/0/1120751276730768/1201390817461565/f) 🎟️

## 🗒️ What

<!--
Briefly list out the changes proposed in this PR.
-->

- Adds two npm scripts in `package.json`:
  - `prettier:check`
  - `prettier:write`
- Updates `prettier.config.js` to set:
  - `useTabs: true`
  - `tabWidth: 2`
- Adds `.prettierignore` file
- Applies new prettier configuration to all files not in `.prettierignore`
- Adds `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file

## 🤷 Why

<!--
Describe why the changes proposed are needed. Some examples: new feature requested, refactor to make things easier later, styling tweaks requested by design, etc.
-->

- We discussed tabs vs. spaces way back in November in a weekly team meeting. The resolution was to test out using tabs instead of spaces, so that is the purpose of this PR.
- Some resources on how tabs are more accessible than spaces:
  - [Why we should default to Tabs instead of Spaces for an 'accessible first' environment](https://dev.to/alexandersandberg/why-we-should-default-to-tabs-instead-of-spaces-for-an-accessible-first-environment-101f)
  - [Tabs vs. Spaces: It's an Accessibility Issue](https://adamtuttle.codes/blog/2021/tabs-vs-spaces-its-an-accessibility-issue/)
  - [Nobody talks about the real reason to use Tabs over Spaces](https://www.reddit.com/r/javascript/comments/c8drjo/nobody_talks_about_the_real_reason_to_use_tabs/)
- Some resources on configuring custom tab widths:
  - [VS Code `editor.tabSize` setting](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/codebasics?ref=hackernoon.com#_indentation)
  - [Managing your tab size rendering preference](https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/setting-up-and-managing-your-personal-account-on-github/managing-personal-account-settings/managing-your-tab-size-rendering-preference) in GitHub
- Adding the new `.prettierignore` file made it easier to run `prettier --write .` without unintended side effects.
- The new `prettier:check` and `prettier:write` npm scripts are purely for convenience of not having to remember what the prettier cli commands look like.
- The new `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file is so the `git blame` ignores the commit where 800+ files were changed, since formatting changes aren't nearly as valuable in a blame as functionality changes. This approach is taken from the [Ignore commits in the blame view](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/using-files/viewing-a-file#ignore-commits-in-the-blame-view) section of GitHub's [Viewing a file](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/using-files/viewing-a-file) article.

## 🛠️ How

<!--
Dive into the approach you took, list resources you referenced, detail other approaches you tried but didn't end up going with, etc.
-->

1. Updated the `prettier.config.js` file
2. Created the `.prettierignore` file
3. Added `prettier:write` npm script
4. Ran `prettier:write` script
5. Later added `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file after some research

## 🧪 Testing

<!--

- [ ] Make sure the changes visually apply as you expect in files

author: dlockhart
body:
Background: We'd like to purge `superagent` from our dependency chain in BSI, as it depends on older versions of libraries that are in conflict with other things in BSI. Also, `superagent` is no longer needed now that browsers support `fetch` natively.

Unfortunately in order to use native fetch, I needed to switch the tests over to run in a browser and not in Node -- which is probably good since this code is intended for the browser anyway. In order to do that, I needed to convert everything to ESM... so this ended up being a breaking change.

Once this merges, I'll be converting `frau-jwt` over to use this directly (and also become ESM) instead of `superagent` and `frau-superagent-xsrf-token`, and then subsequently upgrading BSI things that use it (there are 6).

author: owenv
body:
Reapplying the reverted PR with an extra type annotation which will hopefully allow it to compile with hosttools.

Previously, the removeAll call below the initializer would trigger CoW. If the scratch buffer was larger than the count, this would result in an unnecessarily large allocation. In a very large source file, the source-file-provides-implementation node may have multiple orders of magnitude more edges compared to any other node in the graph, which could lead to excessive memory usage and a large slowdown deallocating the array storage when tearing down the graph.

I tested this using the swiftdeps from an artificially generated swiftdeps with 50k empty struct declarations. Before this change, it took 31s to load and destroy, after this change it only took 0.25s.

## Summary of the changes / Why this improves CrateDB
Add empty `pg_catalog.pg_shdescription` table for improved compatibility with PostgreSQL.
Similiar to `pg_catalog.pg_description`

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/catalog-pg-shdescription.html

---

PostgreSQL 14:
```
postgres=# SELECT * FROM pg_shdescription
postgres-# ;
 objoid | classoid |                description                 
--------+----------+--------------------------------------------
      1 |     1262 | default template for new databases
  14020 |     1262 | unmodifiable empty database
  14021 |     1262 | default administrative connection database
(3 rows)
```

Might become relevant when implementing a `COMMENT` functionality in CrateDB.
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-comment.html

---

e.g. used by Datagrip
```sql
select N.oid::bigint as id,
       datname as name,
       D.description,
       datistemplate as is_template,
       datallowconn as allow_connections,
       pg_catalog.pg_get_userbyid(N.datdba) as "owner"
from pg_catalog.pg_database N
  left join pg_catalog.pg_shdescription D on N.oid = D.objoid
order by case when datname = pg_catalog.current_database() then -1::bigint else N.oid::bigint end
```

body:
## Updates to enable
zwe components install
zwe components enable
zwe components disable
~~zwe internal start~~ to be done in a future pr
zwe internal get-launch-components
zwe internal config get
zwe internal config set
opt-in to configmgr via yaml and cli parm instead of env var.

"set" operations require writing to the left-most config file, and write to parmlib isnt yet supported, just to yaml file.

### note on write operations (components enable, disable, install and internal config set)
 a write is accomplished by configmgr overwriting the left-most config file in the list of config files specified with `-c` such as just one via `-c /path/to/yaml` or multiple via `-c FILE(/path/to/first/yaml):FILE(/path/to/second/yaml)`. This file gets overwritten to contain its original values plus the changes requested. However, this write currently changes strings to be double-quoted and resolves templates. Therefore, you should keep templates out of your first file. Other files in the list can still have templates.

## testing
You can switch between configmgr or not via
* --configmgr on any cli command that has configmgr support (will be ignored on those that dont)
* zowe.useConfigmgr=true within the zowe.yaml

Testing zwe components install:
Try zwe components install --component /path/to/directory/or/pax -c some-zowe-config --configmgr
Observe that the config file you specified now has the component within, and set to "enabled: true".
Also see that the component exists within zowe.extensionDir

Testing zwe components enable:
Try zwe components enable --component-name your-component-name -c some-zowe-config --configmgr
Observe that the config file you specified now has the component as "enabled: true"

Testing zwe components disable:
Try zwe components disable --component-name your-component-name -c some-zowe-config --configmgr
Observe that the config file you specified now has the component as "enabled: false"

Testing zwe internal config get:
Here are some examples to test

zwe internal config get -c "zowe.yaml" --path ".components.app-server.enabled" --configmgr
zwe internal config get -c "zowe.yaml" --path ".components.app-server" --configmgr
zwe internal config get -c "zowe.yaml" --path ".components[]" --configmgr
zwe internal config get -c "zowe.yaml" --path ".components[].enabled" --configmgr

Testing zwe internal config set:
Here are some examples to test. Also test with get commands to see if it worked.

zwe internal config set -c "zowe.yaml" --path ".components.app-server.enabled" --value true --configmgr

Created a new animation feature for camera shaking.

- If there is two animations shaking the camera, only the longer one will prevail.
- Camera shake intensity can be configured at client options. (Also can be disabled).

Long time i promised this feature, sorry, but now there is.

author: jv1i
body:
[MER-1297](https://eliterate.atlassian.net/browse/MER-1297)

### What does it change?

- Attempts to fix the part_mapping view not being refreshed on project publication updates

This replaces `Task.async` for `Task.start`
From the [elixir docs](https://hexdocs.pm/elixir/1.13/Task.html#module-dynamically-supervised-tasks): 

> ..async tasks link the caller and the spawned process. This means that, if the caller crashes, the task will crash too and vice-versa. This is on purpose: if the process meant to receive the result no longer exists, there is no purpose in completing the computation.
>

One reason for the refresh not being executed could be that process running the publication update is finishing before the spawned process that runs the refresh. 

From the[ Task.start docs](https://hexdocs.pm/elixir/1.13/Task.html#start/1) 

>This should only used when the task is used for side-effects (like I/O) and you have no interest on its results nor if it completes successfully.
>
> If the current node is shutdown, the node will terminate even if the task was not completed. For this reason, we recommend to use [Task.Supervisor.start_child/2](https://hexdocs.pm/elixir/1.13/Task.Supervisor.html#start_child/2) instead, which allows you to control the shutdown time via the :shutdown option
>

This fits our use case, since we don't want to depend (or limit) the child process lifetime from the current process. We also don't need to supervise it or shut it down manually, so no need to use `Task.Supervisor.start_child`

Another option would be to use `Task.asnyc_nolink` but it requires a supervisor and we have no intention on supervising the process.

The `Process.sleep/1` call is added as an extra safety measure for cases when the `Publishing.update_publication` is executed inside another transaction. Before refreshing the view, we want all the changes to be persisted.

I didn't manage to replicate the original issue locally, so we agreed on running this in QA to test if this fixes the part_mapping view not being refreshed.

author: rafaqz
body:
This is a huge PR for GeoInterface 1.0 compatability.

It will be breaking for some inputs and details of methods like `rasterize` that use GeoInterface.jl heavily. Notably, the `fill` keyword must always be specified now in `rasterize`, and may contain the feature property name or table column `Symbol`/s or the actual fill value. This means `Symbol` or `Tuple{Symbol}` are not valid values to rasterize, if that would ever make sense anyway. 

Tables with `:geometry` columns (or the first column `GeoInterface.geometrycolumns` returns) are now handled as with other geometries. The preview method of treating each row as a point is also handled for point data.

> In such cases, the alt attribute may be omitted, but one of the following conditions must be met as well:

for case 1, the alt should still be present, just be an empty string.

body:
<!--
  A summary of the change, including any relevant background, motivation, and context.
  If relevant, include a description, screenshots, and/or video of the existing and new behavior.
-->
Currently, we have several tables with unique indexes which aren't working properly and are resulting in duplicate rows. The `code_reviews` table is also susceptible to unwanted duplicate rows, it doesn't have any yet, but we'd like to take care of this issue now before the table gets any bigger. Here's the solution:
- add new virtual columns `open` and `active`
- replace `closed_at` and `deleted_at` in the unique index with these new columns

Before the deploy with this migration, I'll run the query `select count(*) as count_reviews from code_reviews where deleted_at is null and closed_at is null group by user_id, project_id having count_reviews > 1;` in production to ensure that there haven't been any duplicate rows added since this PR and to ensure the unique index can be created.

author: ecarrion
body:
Closes: #7146


# Why

On **Order Creation** we display a loading indicator on the Payments Section to indicate that taxes are being recalculated.
That experience does not fit that well now that **Order Edition** commits all changes immediately and the changes do not necessarily affect taxes.

To mitigate that, this PR:

- Only for **Order Edition**, moves the loading indicator to the right bar button item in the navigation bar, while a remote action is performed.
- Do not show the loading indicator next to the payment section when the order is not-editable.

# Testing instructions

- Navigate to a non-editable order
- Tap the edit button
- Modify the order customer details
- See that the navigation bar shows a loading spinner while the network request is being performed.
- See that there is no loading spinner in the payments section.

# Demo

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/562080/176310450-0728280e-7d63-439d-a612-268a19da34df.mov

Remove `_checkpoint_wrapped_module` prefixes when creating keys for optimizer state_dict.

* **Explanation**: If the type of an `ExplicitCastExpr` is not valid, it is a null type, which causes a crash when checking if the cast type has parameterized existentials. This PR contains a minimal fix for the crash by checking for `nullptr` first.
* **Scope**: Type checking of `is` checks with invalid types in result builders
* **Risk**: Very low, any code that is affected by this changed behavior previously crashed the compiler
* **Testing**: Added regression test case
* **Issue**: rdar://95629905
* **Reviewer**: @xedin on https://github.com/apple/swift/pull/59664
